fuentes: USDA FSIS: Let's Talk Turkey / Happy Thanksgiving / Turkey Basics: Safe Thawing (fridge ~24 h per 4-5 lb; cold water 30 min per lb, change water every 30 min, cook immediately; never thaw on the counter; frozen turkey can be cooked from frozen, ~50% longer)

frases.texto: Your Thanksgiving turkey is frozen solid, and dinner is days away.
frases.estilo: Dry, direct, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Don't leave it on the counter. The USDA says never thaw it there.
The safest way is the fridge: about twenty-four hours for every four to five pounds.
So a sixteen-pound bird needs about three to four days.
frases.estilo: Matter of fact, a little surprised.

frases.texto: Running late? Cold water works: keep it in its wrapper, allow thirty minutes per pound, and change the water every thirty minutes.
Cook it right after a cold-water thaw.
Heads up: you can also cook it from frozen, it just takes about fifty percent longer.
How many days ahead do you start thawing?
Save this, then send it to the friend who thaws the turkey the morning of.
